annotations.title: Is this GitHub repo what it claims?

description: Before you clone, run or trust a GitHub repository (a bot, a tool, an SDK someone sent you): its age and its owner's, commit history (a whole history pushed within an hour is usually a copy), contributors, how many stars arrived each day (bought stars come in a one-day burst), install scripts (and the files they run) and setup.py that download and run code, release downloads that are programs rather than the repo's code, a README handing out password-protected downloads or file-sharing links, CI that runs outside pull requests' code with the repo's secrets or puts issue text into a shell, unpinned actions, a README that asks for a wallet's private key or seed phrase, fork, archived, license, security policy. Verdict: high risk, caution or no warnings, with reasons. Use for 'is this repo legit?', 'is this GitHub bot safe to run?'. Facts about the repository, not its authors.
name: repo_check
title: Is this GitHub repo what it claims?
